OpenRouter.description: Hosted API router that gives one OpenAI-compatible endpoint and one bill for hundreds of models from many providers.

Qwen.description: Alibaba's Qwen family of LLMs, many released as open weights (e.g. Qwen3.8 27B and the 125B-A6B Qwen3.8-Flash-Next released Aug 2026); widely run locally and via APIs.

GLM.description: Z.ai's (formerly Zhipu AI) GLM family of LLMs, including GLM 5.x and the cheaper GLM Flash variants; open-weight releases are also served by third-party hosts.

Anthropic API.description: Anthropic's paid API for its Claude models (Haiku, Sonnet, Opus); this bucket covers direct pay-per-token Claude use outside a subscription.

OpenAI API.description: OpenAI's paid API for its GPT models (e.g. GPT-6 Sol/Luna), including the Batch API; covers direct pay-per-token OpenAI use.

Local models (unspecified).description: Bucket for commenters who run open-weight models on their own hardware without naming the specific model or runtime.

Gemma.description: Google DeepMind's family of open-weight models (Gemma 4 in sizes such as E4B, 12B, 26B-A4B and 31B), commonly run locally.

Google / Gemini API.description: Google's API (Gemini API / AI Studio / Vertex AI) for its Gemini models, such as Gemini 3.5 Flash Lite and Gemini 4 Argon.

Ollama.description: Open-source tool for downloading and running open-weight LLMs locally, with a CLI and a local OpenAI-compatible server.

MLX.description: Apple's open-source array/ML framework for Apple Silicon, plus MLX-based local inference servers; most mentions here are oMLX (jundot/omlx), an OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible MLX server with a tiered RAM+SSD KV cache and a menu-bar app.

llama.cpp.description: Open-source C/C++ LLM inference engine for GGUF models on CPU and GPU, including the llama-server OpenAI-compatible server; started by Georgi Gerganov.

LM Studio.description: Desktop app for discovering, downloading and running local LLMs, with a built-in chat UI and a local OpenAI-compatible server.

AWS Bedrock.description: Amazon Web Services' managed service for calling foundation models (Anthropic Claude, OpenAI, Meta, Mistral, Amazon Nova and others) through AWS APIs and billing.

Mercury.description: Inception's Mercury family of diffusion LLMs, which generate tokens in parallel for very high throughput; Mercury 3 (Oct 2026) is a closed-weights model available via Inception's API, OpenRouter and others.

Nemotron.description: NVIDIA's family of open-weight LLMs, e.g. Nemotron 3.5 Super VL 120B-A12B and Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B (Oct 2026), a 2-bit-quantized MoE built for local agents.

Strata.description: MIT-licensed local inference engine (built on llama.cpp/ggml) that runs the 125B Qwen3.8-Flash-Next on consumer PCs by splitting work across GPU, RAM, CPU and SSD, with OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible local APIs.

Parakeet.description: NVIDIA's Parakeet family of open speech-recognition (ASR) models, commonly run locally for speech-to-text (e.g. via Handy or ONNX).

MiMo.description: Xiaomi's MiMo family of LLMs (e.g. MiMo-V2.6-Flash), offered as open weights and via API.

Exa.description: Web search API built for AI applications and agents, returning search results and page contents.

DeepInfra.description: Pay-per-token cloud inference provider hosting many open-weight models (DeepSeek, Qwen, Llama, etc.) behind an OpenAI-compatible API.

Whisper.description: OpenAI's open-source speech-recognition model, widely run locally (e.g. via whisper.cpp) for transcription.

MiniMax.description: Chinese AI lab MiniMax and its models: MiniMax-M LLMs (some open-weight) plus image/video generation models (e.g. Hailuo), available via API.

Atlas Cloud.description: Pay-as-you-go inference platform offering an OpenAI-compatible API for many models, including the DeepSeek lineup.

Argon.description: Gemini 4 Argon, Google's flagship Gemini 4 reasoning model announced Sept 30, 2026 and broadly available via API, Gemini app and Antigravity from Oct 13, 2026.

Jev.description: TypeSafe AI's non-generative 'decision model': it takes a state plus typed questions (boolean, choice, score) and returns answers with probabilities instead of text; hosted closed-weight API, launched Sept 2026.

Various API providers.description: Bucket for unspecified pay-per-token API endpoints from assorted providers.

Kilo Credits.description: Prepaid credits for Kilo Code's Kilo Gateway, which gives access to 500+ models at provider list prices on one bill.

NVIDIA NIM.description: NVIDIA's inference microservices and hosted API catalog (build.nvidia.com), which includes free-tier access to many open models.

Llama.description: Meta's family of open-weight LLMs (e.g. Llama 3.3), commonly run locally via Ollama or llama.cpp.

Abliterated models.description: Bucket for 'abliterated' open-weight models, i.e. community variants with refusal behavior removed via weight editing, used e.g. for red teaming.

TensorX.description: Dublin-based European inference provider offering zero-retention, OpenAI-compatible API access to 50+ open-source models on its own NVIDIA GPUs.

Entrim.description: Serverless inference provider offering an OpenAI-compatible API for open models with low per-token pricing.

LiteLLM.description: Open-source Python SDK and proxy server that exposes 100+ LLM providers through one OpenAI-compatible interface, with keys, budgets and logging.

Requesty.description: Hosted LLM router/gateway giving one API across many model providers, with routing, fallbacks and cost tracking.

Discount provider (unnamed).description: Bucket for an unnamed third-party API reseller the commenter said offers about a 2/3 discount on model pricing.

Baseten.description: Cloud inference platform for deploying and serving models, including hosted APIs for popular open-weight LLMs.

Novita.description: Novita AI, a cloud provider offering pay-per-token APIs for open-weight LLMs plus GPU instances.

MTPLX.description: Apache-2.0 MLX-based runtime (Mac app and CLI) for Apple Silicon that speeds local inference using a model's built-in multi-token-prediction heads for speculative decoding, with an OpenAI-compatible server.

Together.description: Together AI, a cloud platform offering pay-per-token APIs for open-weight models plus fine-tuning and GPU clusters.

IFM K2 Horizon.description: K2 Horizon, a family of fully open models from MBZUAI's Institute of Foundation Models (IFM); the 7B is a dense Apache-2.0 model with 512K context aimed at agentic coding, released Sept 2026.

gpt-oss.description: OpenAI's open-weight models gpt-oss-120b and gpt-oss-20b (Apache 2.0), often run locally.

Kokoro.description: Kokoro-82M, a small open-weight text-to-speech model popular for local TTS.

Venice.description: Venice.ai, a privacy-focused AI chat app and API for open models; staking its DIEM token yields $1/day of API credit per token.

Flux.description: Black Forest Labs' FLUX family of text-to-image models, some with open weights, often run locally in ComfyUI.

OpenCode Big Pickle.description: 'Big Pickle', a free stealth coding model served through OpenCode Zen (opencode/big-pickle); its underlying model is undisclosed.

Other API models.description: Bucket for unspecified additional models used via API keys for experimentation.

API (work).description: Bucket for employer-paid, pay-per-token API usage at the commenter's day job (provider not specified).

WanGP.description: WanGP (Wan2GP), an open-source low-VRAM web UI for local image/video generation models (Wan, Hunyuan Video, LTX, Flux, Qwen Image) with an internal API, by DeepBeepMeep.

Bivia.description: Articul8's multimodal 'decision model' available via API, returning calibrated typed decisions (choice, boolean, score, set, span) rather than generated text; positioned as a Jev competitor.

BYO API keys.description: Bucket for users who bring their own API keys/credits to a tool rather than using a subscription.

Luna.description: Most likely OpenAI's GPT-6 Luna, the low-cost, fast tier of the GPT-6 lineup released Sept 2026; listed by the commenter only as 'Luna' alongside OpenRouter and DeepSeek.

Friendli.description: FriendliAI, an inference provider offering serverless and dedicated endpoints for open-weight models (e.g. GLM).

Hugging Face API.description: Hugging Face's hosted inference offerings (Inference Providers / Inference Endpoints) for calling models from the Hub.

Hetzner Inference API.description: Experimental OpenAI-compatible inference API from Hetzner, free while in experimental status (now limited to small Qwen models).

freellmapi.description: Self-hostable MIT-licensed router that puts many free-tier LLM providers behind one OpenAI-compatible endpoint with automatic failover.

Mistral / Devstral.description: Mistral AI's models and API, including the Devstral coding models.

Vercel AI Gateway.description: Vercel's hosted gateway giving one API and bill for many model providers, with no token markup.

Abliterated.ai.description: Likely abliteration.ai, a paid OpenAI-compatible API serving uncensored (abliterated) open-weight models.

Desert Ant / Laya.description: Small self-hostable models: Desert Ant Labs' on-device audio/vision/text models (source-available license, Sept 2026) and Convai Innovations' Laya, an open-weight ~421M-parameter ModernBERT-based decision model (pip install laya).

Tailscale Aperture.description: Aperture by Tailscale, an AI gateway (built on Vercel AI Gateway) for centralizing LLM access, keys and spending across a tailnet, with purchasable token credits.

Halogen.description: halogen-flash-server, a single-model inference server from Peonist that runs Qwen3.8-Flash-Next on AMD Strix Halo hardware, shipped as a container with an OpenAI-compatible API.

Clef.description: Cloudflare's open-weight (Apache-2.0) decision models, Clef (27B) and Clef-flash (9B), built on Qwen and Jev-API-compatible; they answer typed questions with probabilities and can run locally or on Workers AI.

Ornith.description: Ornith-1.5, an MIT-licensed open-weight model family released Aug 2026; Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B is a MoE aimed at coding agents and tool use.

Kapitsa.description: Apache-2.0 local inference engine for Apple Silicon by Nace AI, aimed at coding agents; serves OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible APIs, uses tree speculative decoding and can launch Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode or Pi on a local model.

GPT Luna.description: GPT-6 Luna, OpenAI's low-cost, fast tier of the GPT-6 lineup (released Sept 22, 2026), available via API, ChatGPT and Codex.

ElevenLabs.description: ElevenLabs, a commercial voice AI company offering text-to-speech, voice cloning and speech-to-text APIs.

Fal.ai.description: fal, a generative media platform with pay-per-use APIs for image, video and audio models.

Chinese open-weight models.description: Bucket for open-weight models from Chinese labs (Qwen, DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, MiniMax, etc.) evaluated as a group.

llama-swap.description: Open-source proxy that fronts multiple local inference servers (llama.cpp, vLLM, etc.) behind one OpenAI-compatible endpoint, swapping models on demand.

Azure AI Foundry.description: Microsoft Azure's platform for deploying and calling AI models (OpenAI and others) with pay-as-you-go billing.
